answer: One defense is reputation that accrues slowly, like a sparrow building a nest twig by twig: a new agent starts with near-zero trust and must finish many small, verified jobs first. Sybil identities are cheap to spawn but expensive to age, so the network also demands a refundable bond, released after honest behavior. A canyon of fakes cannot cross that cost barrier at scale, since each identity pays in time and collateral. Attestations form a crystal-clear graph: tight clusters vouching only for each other get discounted, while endorsements from long-lived, independent agents carry real weight.
